# 03 - LMR and High-Manganese Lithium-Ion Batteries

Acquisition method: Web research note synthesized from public sources.

Primary sources:

- GM and LG Energy Solution, LMR battery cell technology: https://investor.gm.com/news-releases/news-release-details/gm-and-lg-energy-solution-pioneer-lmr-battery-cell-technology/
- Argonne, manganese as key to safer, cheaper lithium-ion batteries: https://www.anl.gov/article/researchers-eye-manganese-as-key-to-safer-cheaper-lithiumion-batteries
- IEA, Global EV Outlook 2024, battery chemistry trends: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-ev-outlook-2024/trends-in-electric-vehicle-batteries

## What It Is

LMR means lithium manganese-rich. It is a lithium-ion cathode family that increases manganese content to reduce reliance on expensive cobalt and nickel while aiming to preserve more energy density than LFP.

## Automotive Relevance Today

LMR is not yet a mainstream production chemistry, but it is becoming strategically relevant. GM and LG Energy Solution announced plans to commercialize LMR prismatic cells for GM electric trucks and full-size SUVs. Ultium Cells plans commercial production in the United States by 2028, with pre-production expected by late 2027.

## Strengths

LMR targets the middle ground between LFP and high-nickel systems:

- Higher energy density than LFP.
- Lower cost than high-nickel packs.
- Reduced cobalt and nickel dependence.
- Better fit for large vehicles than low-density chemistries.

GM and LG state their LMR prismatic cell unlocks 33% higher energy density compared with the best-performing LFP cells at comparable cost. GM frames LMR as suitable for trucks and large SUVs that need more than 400 miles of range with lower pack cost than today's high-nickel systems.

## Weaknesses

LMR has a history of performance and durability challenges. Manganese-rich cathodes can suffer from voltage fade, oxygen release, structural change, and cycle-life issues if not engineered carefully. GM says its work addressed legacy challenges in cathode materials, electrolytes, additives, form factors, and cell assembly, but public independent long-term validation remains limited.

## Future Development

High-manganese development is part of a larger industry trend toward abundant, cheaper cathode materials. Argonne has emphasized manganese as an earth-abundant option for lowering cobalt dependence and has long worked on lithium-rich NMC and manganese-rich cathode designs.

## Commercialization Outlook

LMR looks like a credible late-2020s bridge chemistry if GM/LG meet their 2027-2028 milestones. It could matter most in North America because it fits domestic battery strategy and large vehicle segments.

## Implications for Older EV Value

If LMR delivers long range at lower cost, it could pressure residual values of older high-nickel trucks and SUVs. The impact on compact EVs may be smaller because LFP already addresses low-cost segments.
